title: Introduce late-fusion pivot reranker and adaptive-quant routing for low-latency multilingual serving
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The current cross-encoder rerank endpoint offers good quality but struggles to meet 95th-percentile latency targets for certain low-resource locales and tail queries. Full-precision cross-encoders provide higher quality but are expensive in tokens/latency; aggressively quantized variants are cheaper but risk regressions for some languages.

This ticket proposes a two-part approach: (1) a late-fusion 'pivot' reranker that combines a fast lexical/sparse signal with a compact cross-encoder score only when needed, and (2) adaptive-quant routing: run-time selection of a quantization variant (FP16 / 8-bit / 4-bit) based on per-request latency budget, locale confidence, and model health signals. Goal: preserve >98% of quality delta on benchmark prompts while reducing p95 latency by >=20% for target low-latency SLAs and lowering unit cost on average by ~18%.
acceptance_criteria: Late-fusion pivot reranker implemented in endpoint with config flag (feature-gated)
Adaptive-quant routing selects model variant at request time and falls back safely to FP16 on quality outlier detection
E2E benchmarks: p50 and p95 latency improvement >=20% for configured low-latency workspace; overall rerank MRR drop <2% on multilingual eval set
Canary harness and per-locale smoke tests added to regression suite and run in CI
Playbook documenting when to enable late-fusion and routing thresholds; rollout plan verified with product and SRE
tasks: Prototype late-fusion scoring: implement lexical BM25-lite + normalized cross-encoder score combiner (Arjun)
Instrument runtime routing signals: request latency budget, locale tag, recent model-quality anomalies (Maya)
Integrate quant-variants into model catalog and on-the-fly selector (engine/runtime) (Tess)
Build canary: 1% traffic split, per-locale metrics, alerting on quality regressions (SLO board) (Leo)
Add regression test vectors for low-resource locales and synthetic adversarial pairs (QA)
Run offline A/B on logged queries to estimate quality/latency tradeoffs before rollout (Data Science)
Write rollout playbook + rollback criteria and link to dashboard (Docs/Product)
Post-rollout monitoring: KV warm-start hit rate, model fallback frequency, per-token cost delta (SRE)
Security review: verify no PII leakage changes and that routing metadata obeys RBAC (Security)
Schedule cross-team review with Product & Solutions to confirm customer-facing behavior (Maya)
comments: 2026-02-28 -- Maya Chen: Created ticket after spike — saw consistent p95 latency spikes for fr- and pt- locale rerank traffic when candidate pools >80. Proposed late-fusion to reduce reliance on heavy cross-encoder scoring for easy cases.

2026-03-03 -- Arjun Patel: Prototype late-fusion implemented in local dev harness. Initial offline test shows that for ~42% of candidate lists the lexical-only ranker matches top-1 from full cross-encoder; fusion reduces average runtime xformer calls by ~37%.

2026-03-05 -- Tess Nguyen: Added 8-bit quant variant to model catalog. Preliminary accuracy hit on en/devset is ~1.1% MRR; for some low-resource languages the hit is up to 3.8% — need routing heuristics.

2026-03-07 -- Data Science (Sofia Ruiz): Ran offline A/B on month of prod logs. Simulated adaptive routing (budget-based) reduces p95 by estimated 18% and lowers compute cost by ~16% while keeping MRR loss under 1.7% overall when late-fusion enabled for high-confidence lexical cases.

2026-03-10 -- Leo Park: Canary harness ready. Wiring dashboard: rerank.p95, rerank.mrr, fallback.rate, per-locale.delta. Alert thresholds proposed: delta_mrr > 2.5% for >10 minutes or fallback_rate > 5% for >5 minutes.

2026-03-12 -- Security (Aisha Khan): Reviewed routing metadata. No additional PII surfaced; must ensure locale tags not derived from user text without consent in EU customers — added label 'privacy-review' for affected workspaces.
2026-03-14 -- Arjun Patel: Integration tests green locally. Starting 1% canary rollout in staging tomorrow. Next: collect canary traces and run smoke-suite against en, fr, pt, ja, es locales.
